description: The chart illustrates the measured “effect” of context masking on case tasks across language families, with variability shown via error bars (standard deviation), and it displays six model configurations per family. The horizontal axis contains the categorical language-family groups ordered left to right as IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic; the vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (the plotted range extends slightly below 0 and up to the mid-30s). In each family, six adjacent bars appear in a consistent color/legend mapping: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). For IE-Baltic, the bars are small and positive at roughly ~2 (mBERT-L₂), ~1 (XLM-L₂), ~3 (mBERT-R₂), ~3 (XLM-R₂), ~6 (mBERT-B₂), and ~5 (XLM-B₂), each with modest error bars; for IE-Germanic, mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ are around ~10 each, mBERT-R₂ is near ~0, XLM-R₂ is slightly below 0, and the B₂ bars are around ~15 (pink) and ~15 (red) with larger error bars; for IE-Indic, the L₂ bars are near ~1 and ~0, the R₂ bars are high at about ~20 (light green) and ~18 (dark green), and the B₂ bars are higher at about ~24 (pink) and ~21 (red), all with comparatively large error bars; for IE-Romance, values are around ~6 (mBERT-L₂), ~4 (XLM-L₂), ~5 (mBERT-R₂), ~1 (XLM-R₂), ~12 (mBERT-B₂), and ~6 (XLM-B₂); for IE-Slavic, the L₂ bars are about ~10 (light blue) and ~9 (dark blue), the R₂ bars are near ~1 (light green) and ~0 (dark green), and the B₂ bars are about ~17 (pink) and ~15 (red), with moderate-to-large error bars; for IE-other, the L₂ bars are around ~6 each, the R₂ bars are near ~0 (light green) and slightly below 0 (dark green), and the B₂ bars are around ~8 (pink) and ~8 (red); for Isolate, all bars cluster close to zero with small positive values around ~0 to ~2; for Semitic, mBERT-L₂ is around ~11, XLM-L₂ around ~16, mBERT-R₂ is slightly below 0, XLM-R₂ is around ~0 to slightly below 0, mBERT-B₂ is around ~15, and XLM-B₂ is around ~19, with notably large error bars in this family; for Uralic, all bars are near zero (roughly ~0 to ~2) with small error bars. The bars are grouped by family (not stacked), there is no visible sorting by magnitude within families beyond the fixed model order, and no individual bars appear specially highlighted beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars.
caption_used: The bar chart depicts the effect of context masking on case tasks, segmented by language family, with error bars representing the standard deviation. The horizontal axis categorizes language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, while the vertical axis quantifies the 'effect' on a linear scale from 0 to 40. Six model configurations—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—are represented by distinct bars in each category, color-coded as light blue, dark blue, light green, dark green, pink, and red, respectively. The IE-Indic family demonstrates the highest variability, with effects approximately ranging from 15 to 28, while the Uralic family consistently exhibits minimal effects, barely surpassing 2. Notably, the Semitic group shows a pronounced negative effect for the XLM-B₂ model, plummeting to roughly -12, whereas other models in this group stabilize around 15. In the IE-Germanic family, the mBERT-L₂ configuration consistently exceeded the XLM-L₂ model by a margin of approximately 5 units. The IE-Romance family displays a relatively uniform effect across models, with values clustering around 10, while the IE-Slavic family reveals a marked decline in performance for the XLM-R₂ model, which lags behind mBERT-R₂ by nearly 8 units. Error bars indicate substantial variability in the Semitic and IE-Indic families, particularly for the XLM-based models.
